title: Foreign Travel Emergency Benefit Terms Across the Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan Letters
content:
Emergency care received outside the United States is a benefit only certain plan letters of Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies carry. Where a letter carries it, the benefit is written on three terms: a deductible taken each calendar year on that care, the share of the care the policy pays after that deductible, and a maximum the policy will pay on that benefit over the whole life of the policy. All amounts are in USD.

| Policy | Foreign travel emergency care | Yearly deductible | Share paid after the deductible | Lifetime maximum |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan A | not covered | 0.00 | 0 per cent | 0.00 |
| Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan B | not covered | 0.00 | 0 per cent | 0.00 |
| Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan D | covered | 250.00 | 80 per cent | 50000.00 |
| Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan K | not covered | 0.00 | 0 per cent | 0.00 |
| Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan N | covered | 250.00 | 80 per cent | 50000.00 |
| Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan G | covered | 250.00 | 80 per cent | 50000.00 |
| Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement High Deductible Plan G | covered | 250.00 | 80 per cent | 50000.00 |

### Basis Q and A

*On which letters does this benefit exist at all?* On Plan D, Plan N, Plan G and High Deductible Plan G. On Plan A, Plan B and Plan K the benefit is not carried, and each of its three terms stands at 0.00 or 0 per cent accordingly.

*Do the four letters that carry it differ from one another?* They do not. Each takes a yearly deductible of 250.00 on that care, pays 80 per cent of it after that deductible, and will pay no more than 50000.00 on the benefit over the life of the policy.

*What is the lifetime maximum measured over?* The whole life of the policy, not a calendar year; the yearly deductible, by contrast, is taken each calendar year.
